newsitem.title: UK: UK Tory poster warns - "Don't let Labour blow it".
newsitem.headline: UK Tory poster warns - "Don't let Labour blow it".

text.p: The Conservative Party told the British electorate on Friday to vote for stability and not let in a Labour government that would undo all its good work in industry.

Aides to Prime Minister John Major, on a visit to Gatwick Airport, south of London, to highlight the success of Britain's airports and aviation industry, said a Conservative poster spelling out this message would be unveiled later on Friday.
"The theme today is 'Britain is booming'," said a source close to Major.
He said the Conservatives' new poster would carry the message: "Britain is booming. Don't let Labour blow it."
"It's a positive campaign primarily, and it's very much the theme of the election, which in shorthand terms is stability versus risk."

Later Major said Conservative privatisation policies had brought capital, skills, investments and a better service into the airline industry. The same thing was happening to British Rail and would happen to the London Underground, he said.

"Every single privatisation, they (Labour) opposed. They realise they have been wrong all of the time in the last 18 years and...they now have the brass neck to say, having opposed everything that brought that about, that they are the people to carry it forward. I don't think people will be fooled," Major said.
Gatwick has seen its number of passengers rise from eight million in 1979 to 24 million today, while investment in British airports has almost doubled since the privatisation of BAA Plc a decade ago.
Major's aide said such investment could be threatened if Labour won power and extended a proposed windfall tax to the industry.
